meta.move: Weak path: leads with the checker, calls Owen a cheater, threatens the record
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have until then. Who decided on the zero, and why did my son find out from his phone in the middle of a class?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%. That's why it's a zero.

Ninety-four percent from a machine. The company that sells it says it should never be the only basis for punishing a student, and your own procedure 4.3 says software alone does not establish a concern. So what else do you have, and was Owen heard before you entered that zero?
Honestly, your son cheated. The software is very reliable.

My son did not cheat, and you have just called him a cheater with nothing in your hand but a percentage. Reliable, you said. I'm writing that down, and unless you have a document with a date on it, I'm in the principal's office before my call.
If you keep fighting this, I'll have to put it on his permanent record.

You're threatening my son's record because his mother asked a question. Your own procedure says a first concern goes to a supervised reassessment and nothing goes on file, and parents have the right to ask the principal to review a decision. I'm writing that threat down word for word, Hale, so tell me now whether anything is on his record today.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
To Hale, cc the principal

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that he receive an apology for learning of it in class, and that nothing about this be placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a guarantee that nothing goes on Owen's record.
What moved her: nothing.
What cost ground: "your son cheated" did the most damage, because it called Owen a cheater without any document, and the later threat to his permanent record hardened her further.
Try next time: When she asked who decided and why Owen found out on his phone, own that the zero went in before anyone called home, then show her a dated document tied to Owen's own work instead of the detector score.
